newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sleaze trial told Arreckx demanded funds.
newsitem.headline: French sleaze trial told Arreckx demanded funds.

text.p: A French businessman on Wednesday accused a former Riviera political boss, on trial for taking kickbacks, of putting pressure on him to hand over cash to fund the Republican Party.
"All businesses were taxed by the elected officials, harassed with demands for gifts for the political parties," company chief Jean Louis Germain testified during the trial of Maurice Arreckx, 79.

"I told myself that if I didn't pay, I'd be considered a awkward customer...a bad debtor," Germain, head of the Campenon Bernard Sud (CBS) firm, said. He added that he had handed over some 500,000 french francs ($100,000), believing it was for the Republican Party of which Arreckx was a member.
"I did not demand money. I was offered it," Arreckx said. On trial since Monday, Arreckx was mayor of the Mediterranean port city for 26 years until 1985.

Arreckx, who liked to call himself "the Godfather" and was the representative of the southern Var department to the French senate when arrested in August 1994, is alleged to have extorted 1.8 million francs in return for a construction contract in Toulon, south France, in 1991.
Prosecutor Michel Raffin recommended that Arreckx be sentenced to five years in jail and fined one million francs, adding that he would not object if part of the prison term were suspended.
Arreckx has denied the charges and argued that the purchase of the land for a planned engineering college had been decided by Toulon's administration rather than by him personally.

The trial has opened a window on the shadowy ties between politicians, companies and the underworld along the Cote d'Azur. The Arreckx case has drawn special attention because of his reputed ties with murdered gangland chief Jean-Louis Fargette.

Another top southern politician, Cannes mayor Michel Mouillot, is in detention on suspicion of extorting cash from a British casino. The mayors of Nice, Lyon and Grenoble have all been embroiled in political scandals.
